arxiv-1706-08269.title: Top-down Transformation Choice
arxiv-1706-08269.creator: Torsten Hothorn Universität Zürich
arxiv-1706-08269.description: Abstract \Plainauthor Hothorn \Plaintitle Top-Down Transformation Choice \Shorttitle Top-Down Transformation Choice \Abstract Simple models are preferred over complex models, but over-simplistic models could lead to erroneous interpretations. The classical approach is to start with a simple model, whose shortcomings are assessed in residual-based model diagnostics.

arxiv-2104-01748.description: Abstract This paper studies the quantitative unique continuation for a semi-linear parabolic-elliptic coupled system on a bounded domain Ω \Omega . This system is a simplified version of the chemotaxis model introduced by Keller and Segel in [ 14 ] .

arxiv-2105-05028.title: Are rare rogue fluctuations generic to strongly nonlinear and non-integrable systems?
arxiv-2105-05028.creator: Rahul Kashyap, Surajit Sen
arxiv-2105-05028.description: Abstract Extensive dynamical simulations are used to explore the possible existence of sudden sufficiently large energy or rogue fluctuations (RF) at late times and across short time windows in the strongly nonlinear regime of the β \beta -Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou (FPUT) type systems.

arxiv-2107-12552.title: Estimating high-dimensional Markov-switching VARs
arxiv-2107-12552.description: Abstract Abstract: Maximum likelihood estimation of large Markov-switching vector autoregressions (MS-VARs) can be challenging or infeasible due to parameter proliferation. To accommodate situations where dimensionality may be of comparable order to or exceeds the sample size, we adopt a sparse framework and propose two penalized maximum likelihood estimators with either the Lasso or the smoothly clipped absolute deviation (SCAD) penalty.

arxiv-2205-05863.title: Quasi-static decomposition and the Gibbs factorial in small thermodynamic systems Journal: Journal of Statistical Physics
arxiv-2205-05863.creator: Shin-ichi Sasa and Ken Hiura and Naoko Nakagawa and Akira Yoshida
arxiv-2205-05863.description: Abstract For small thermodynamic systems in contact with a heat bath, we determine the free energy by imposing the following two conditions. First, the quasi-static work in any configuration change is equal to the free energy difference. Second, the temperature dependence of the free energy satisfies the Gibbs-Helmholtz relation.

arxiv-2208-01071.title: Multidimensional dissipative solitons and solitary vortices
arxiv-2208-01071.creator: B. A. Malomed
arxiv-2208-01071.description: Abstract This article offers a review of (chiefly, theoretical) results for self-trapped states (solitons) in two- and three-dimensional (2D and 3D) models of nonlinear dissipative media. The existence of such solitons requires to maintain two stable balances: between nonlinear self-focusing and linear spreading (diffraction and/or dispersion) of the physical fields, and between losses and gain in the medium.

arxiv-2311-05094.title: Fast Combinatorial Algorithms for Efficient Sortation
arxiv-2311-05094.creator: Madison Van DykKim Klause, Jochen Koenemann, Nicole Megow
arxiv-2311-05094.description: Abstract Modern parcel logistic networks are designed to ship demand between given origin, destination pairs of nodes in an underlying directed network. Efficiency dictates that volume needs to be consolidated at intermediate nodes in typical hub-and-spoke fashion. In practice, such consolidation requires parcel sortation.

arxiv-2405-16146.title: Dual-Adapter: Training-free Dual Adaptation for Few-shot Out-of-Distribution Detection
arxiv-2405-16146.creator: Xinyi Chen, Yaohui Li, Haoxing Chen
arxiv-2405-16146.description: Abstract We study the problem of few-shot out-of-distribution (OOD) detection, which aims to detect OOD samples from unseen categories during inference time with only a few labeled in-domain (ID) samples. Existing methods mainly focus on training task-aware prompts for OOD detection.

arxiv-2406-13047.title: Symplectic Representation of the Ginzburg-Landau Theory
arxiv-2406-13047.creator: E.A. Reis 1,2 , G.X.A. Petronilo 1,3 , R.G.G. Amorim 1,4,8 H. Belich 5 , F.C. Khanna 6,7 , A.E. Santana
arxiv-2406-13047.description: Abstract In this work, the Ginzburg-Landau theory is represented on a symplectic manifold with a phase space content. The order parameter is defined by a quasi-probability amplitude, which gives rise to a quasi-probability distribution function, i.e., a Wigner-type function. The starting point is the thermal group representation of Euclidean symmetries and gauge symmetry.

arxiv-2503-05596.title: Bridging Classical and Quantum String Matching: A Computational Reformulation of Bit-Parallelism
arxiv-2503-05596.creator: Simone Faro, Arianna Pavone, Caterina Viola
arxiv-2503-05596.description: Abstract String matching is a fundamental problem in computer science, with critical applications in text retrieval, bioinformatics, and data analysis. Among the numerous solutions that have emerged for this problem in recent decades, bit-parallelism has significantly enhanced their practical efficiency, leading to the development of several optimized approaches for both exact and approximate string matching.

arxiv-2505-14615.title: SATBench: Benchmarking LLMs’ Logical Reasoning via Automated Puzzle Generation from SAT Formulas
arxiv-2505-14615.creator: Anjiang Wei, Yuheng Wu, Yingjia Wan, Tarun Suresh, Huanmi Tan, Zhanke Zhou, Sanmi Koyejo, Ke Wang, Alex Aiken
arxiv-2505-14615.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Anjiang Wei, Yuheng Wu, Yingjia Wan, Tarun Suresh, Huanmi Tan, Zhanke Zhou, Sanmi Koyejo, Ke Wang, Alex Aiken. We introduce SATBench, a benchmark for evaluating the logical reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs) through logical puzzles derived from Boolean satisfiability (SAT) problems.

pmc-12570832.title: Hybridization of Lycium qingshuiheense and L. ningxiaense revealed using morphological, SSR markers, and chloroplast genomic data
pmc-12570832.creator: Lei Zhang, Chaopan Zhang, Erdong Zhang, Yuqing Wei, Guoqi Zheng
pmc-12570832.description: BackgroundLycium has economic and ecological significance, but its natural hybridization has received little attention. Lycium qingshuiheense and L. ningxiaense exhibit intermediate morphological traits between or blended with L. barbarum and L. ruthenicum, inferring their potential hybrid origin. To clarify this hypothesis, the present study investigated their hybridization using morphological traits, nuclear simple sequence repeats (SSRs) markers, and chloroplast genomic data.

pmc-12589898.creator: Takuma Inagawa, Hajime Ariga, Hiroki Okano, Takako Enokida, Takashi Usami, Atsushi Unuma, Yuji Saitoh, Naoko Satake, Takamasa Noda
pmc-12589898.description: AimTo identify the factors associated with the severity and prognosis of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID‐19) in patients with psychiatric or neurological disorders.MethodsWe retrospectively analyzed the clinical characteristics and treatment outcomes of 349 patients with those disorders who were admitted for COVID‐19 at the National Center of Neurology and Psychiatry between June 2020 and March 2023.

pmc-12614394.title: Dynamic Assessment of Fine Motor Control and Vocalization in Parkinson Disease Through a Smartphone App: Cross-Sectional Study of Time-Severity Interaction Effects
pmc-12614394.creator: Youho Myong, Seo Jung Yun, Kyudong Park, Byung-Mo Oh, Han Gil Seo, Lorraine Buis
pmc-12614394.description: BackgroundParkinson disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by motor and nonmotor symptoms that worsen over time, significantly impacting quality of life. While clinical evaluations such as the Unified Parkinson’s Disease Rating Scale (UPDRS) are standard for assessing disease severity, they offer somewhat limited temporal resolution and are susceptible to observer variability.

pmc-12652121.title: Membrane Lipids and Osmolytes Rearrangements Under Cell Wall Stress in Aspergillus niger
pmc-12652121.creator: Elena A Ianutsevich, Olga A Danilova, Sofiya A Saharova, Vera M Tereshina, Makoto Kimura
pmc-12652121.description: The cell wall integrity pathway is activated in response to cell wall stress (CWS). The defense system in aspergilli employs three transcription factors—RlmA, MsnA, and CrzA—which also facilitate adaptation to various abiotic stressors and involve alterations in cytosolic osmolyte composition and membrane lipid profiles. However, their role in adaptation to CWS remains unclear.

uslaw-usc-t7-s9033.title: 7 U.S.C. § 9033 — Term of loans
uslaw-usc-t7-s9033.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t7-s9033.description: United States Code, Title 7 (Agriculture); Chapter 115 (Agricultural Commodity Policy And Programs); Subchapter II (Marketing Loans). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Term of loan In the case of each loan commodity, a marketing assistance loan under section 9031 of this title shall have a term of 9 months beginning on the first day of the first month after the month.
